To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CP and EV exposure altered the expression of cytokine genes but not the ability of juvenile Chinook salmon to survive IHNV exposure, and that the combination of CP and EV with IHNV exposure led to synergistic effects on TGF-beta expression in spleen and IGF- 1 transcription in spleens of fish.

CP, EV, and IHNV exposure, singly and in combination (CP/IHNV and/or EV/IHNV), did not synergistically impair the ability of juvenile Chinook salmon to survive a subsequent IHNV infection, but the combined exposure to EV/IHNV led to increased transcription of IL-1beta and TGF-beta in the spleen and Mx protein in kidney, whereas CP/IHNV exposure led to increased transcription levels of Mx protein in the spleen.

the insecticides chlorpyrifos and esfenvalerated did not synergize IHNV-induced mortality in Chinook salmon, but they did affect the expression of immune-regulatory cytokines in the spleen and kidney.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of pesticides, a pathogen and their combination on the expression of immune-regulatory cytokines in juvenile Chinook Salmon.

the combined effects of two pesticides (insecticides), which are used extensively in agriculture, forestry, and aquaculture, and IHNV, which is a pathogen of major economic importance to the salmon industry.
the effects of pesticides on fish immune function, and how these effects might influence the susceptibility of fish to disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CP and EV did not synergize with IHNV to increase mortality.
exposure of juvenile Chinook salmon to CP or EV, singly or in combination with IHNV, does not lead to increased mortality, but does lead to changes in immune-related gene expression.
the immune response of fish is altered by exposure to insecticides and IHNV, and that this may have long-term consequences for the fish.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
exposure to CP, EV and IHNV singly or in combination does not affect fish survival, but the immune system of the fish is affected by these stressors.
CP and EV did not affect the ability of Chinook salmon to survive IHNV, and that the combined exposure to CP and IHNV, and EV and IHNV did not result in increased mortality.
exposure to CP and EV, singly and in combination with IHNV, did not impair survival, but altered cytokine expression in a time- and tissue-dependent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sublethal concentrations can affect the expression of immune-regulatory cytokines in fish.
the effects of environmental stressors on fish immune function can be complex, and that it is not always possible to predict the outcome of combined exposure to pollutants and pathogens.
sublethal concentrations CP and EV do not synergize the effects of IHNV in Chinook salmon.
